design: Frozen retrospective benchmark. Structural combination weights were fit on these labels; the scorer is not a roster-to-label table.
primaryDefinition: Complete ten exact known champions in draft-phase-only extracts; no detected draft-process, player/team-strength, meta or result-aware reason. Conservative keyword screening is imperfect.
broaderDefinition: All nonconflicting draft-phase stated labels with complete rosters, including historical-context reasons and independently supplied dossier rosters for originally incomplete extracts.
limitations: The method, champion taxonomy and rules were distilled from overlapping Kazewa videos. This is not an independent holdout and does not establish future fidelity.
The primary screening uses explicit keywords; unobserved context can remain and some composition-only reasoning can be excluded conservatively.
Reconstructed rosters in the broader cohort come from existing project dossier headers and answer keys, not a newly verified external match feed.
Broadcast left/right are anonymized as blue/red for exact-extract cases; the engine cannot use first-pick or map-side advantages.
Predictions of Kazewa preference and predictions of actual match winners are distinct outcomes.
The structural combination weights were fit on these same retrospective labels. Agreement on this file is not an independent test, and 70% does not pass the 85% fidelity gate.

Sivir is an instant win: ricochets off two tanks, spell shield blocks Viktor laser
HLE outscales and outfights mid/late; Gen.G must snowball through bot-side priority with Skarner and Bard

cases.label: Gen.G dominated the Fearless draft
reasons: HLE banning Braum and leaving Yunara gave Gen.G a free first-pick hypercarry with no counterplay
HLE's early Aurora checkmated themselves and let Gen.G secure Alistar
Nocturne has no good target: K'Sante and Alistar neutralise his ult, Yunara can dash out
Gen.G kept too many options (tanks, Nidalee, TF) while HLE was forced into tank top/support
TF mid gives Gen.G priority to follow Nidalee and shut down Nocturne; Camille support fears lane swaps

cases.label: Gen.G on draft; Poppy too strong
reasons: Zeri is a good answer to short-range Lucian-Nami
Zac into K'Sante adds nothing; T1 should have picked Gwen again, which might have flipped his pick to T1
Xin Zhao is weak into Corki and Zeri
Poppy is too strong against Xin, Zac and Lucian-Nami; Annie and Corki are very strong

cases.label: Draft strongly favors HLE
reasons: Right reused the Aurora-Nocturne combo; left answered with a tank (Sion) and Gnar
He strongly prefers left so far, with right facing the same Ezreal/Kalista problem as game 1
With Varus + Renata, he does not see how right beats the left
Twitch last pick is surprising; Twitch is weaker than Varus at pro level but can work in swap meta and was a surprise

cases.label: HLE draft slightly better than T1
reasons: Senna-Nautilus answer is smart: good long-range comp and a pick-away from T1's favorite bot duo
Rek'Sai is very strong into all three T1 carries (TF, Corki, Jinx) with unavoidable flash-knockup
HLE has a block of four with double range, disengage and tank, plus a Rek'Sai/Xin Zhao duo
Jinx + Rell want to dive, which wants mid priority, so Corki is a poor fit; Taliyah would be ideal but was banned
T1 scales with TF side lane and resets; HLE has more early pressure and map control

cases.label: T1 global ultimates and tank win
reasons: HLE's double-tank start with Nautilus is a bad pick-away with anti-synergy
Zeri is a bad pick: no range, no damage in this draft
T1 has multiple global ultimates (TF, Sion, Nocturne, Corki package) while HLE has none
Without K'Sante HLE cannot hold Sion; T1 also has the strongest tank
Jax is a real counter to TF and Doran is a great Jax player, so HLE keeps some chance

cases.label: G2 full early synergy, Fnatic no identity
reasons: G2 side is one coherent full-snowball identity: jungle frontline, defensive top, aggressive mid, Draven/Leona bot able to dive
Fnatic side has zero synergy: scaling Ivern, a disengage top tank, Taliyah with no follow-up, safe Xayah and a Nautilus that wants to accelerate
Fnatic banned Azir instead of picking it, even though Azir is what won them an earlier game
Blind-pick Taliyah plus a tank top instead of a real carry top (Olaf/Fiora) wasted Ivern's hypercarry value
Fnatic showed their Ornn hover, revealing the last pick to G2; draft looked unprepared

cases.label: T1 wins mid and bot
reasons: Azir vs Taliyah: having Azir wins mid
Zeri out-pushes Ezreal and holds permanent prio bot
Alistar only works in a dive/anchor comp and right has none, so it will suffer
Right comp is good in lane phase but does not scale and has nothing to push/peel against
Skarner vs K'Sante is similar but Skarner is stronger; left comp is curved but fine for T1

cases.label: PSG wins top side, bot even
reasons: BDS banning Jarvan IV while leaving Maokai was a big mistake; their mobile picks did not fear Jarvan
BDS committed the jungle too early instead of keeping flexible tank answers to Maokai
Azir into Jayce is a known losing matchup; Jayce will beat Azir
Kennen will farm freely, Adam forced onto a tank (Sion) which is not his strength
Top side (first three picks) clearly favours PSG, bot lane roughly even
BDS usually wins via top-side leads and cannot here

cases.label: BDS trolled draft, PSG wins it
reasons: Renekton is one of the worst first picks; BDS also failed to ban Kennen despite prep
Kalista + Nautilus is a cheesy error; Nautilus adds little value
Renekton plus Taliyah in the same draft is a combination that never wins; Taliyah has no jungle synergy
PSG has a tank jungle (Poppy) that is strong because most tanks were removed, plus a strong 1-3-1 with Jax/Akali
Jax beats Renekton as the game goes on; Azir in blind would have fixed BDS's Nashor setup
He ends with roughly even but right scaling a bit more

exploratoryRaw.name: Exploratory full-review corpus, kept separate from draft-phase benchmark
limitations: Explicit late opinions are excluded, but absence of a late flag is not proof of a pregame judgment. Full-review extraction can retain hindsight and omitted timing context.
Cases conflicting with matched clean draft-phase labels, including an explicit absence of preference, are excluded.
Game numbers restart in multi-series reviews. Clean matches use unambiguous known-pick correspondence; unresolved matches remain marked and cannot establish independence.
Some cases overlap the clean benchmark or method source. This cohort never contributes to the fidelity gate.

cases.label: KC draft finally makes sense
reasons: KC: Maokai first pick removes many immobile and dash champions; strong scaling tank + several damage dealers
KC: triple carry (TF, Tristana, Kai'Sa) behind Maokai - once at 3 items fights and Nash go very fast
Tristana chosen to match Azir; banning Taliyah removed BDS's usual answer
BDS: Ivern to empower Adam's top side, but Yasuo is not a real answer to Canna's TF and lacks setup (no Gragas-type knock-up)
BDS should have punished Maokai with Karthus/Sivir or Morgana; Zeri lacks range
only caveat: TF blind is fine because the player is Canna; with a weaker top it would be risky

cases.label: Nocturne first pick hands T1 the draft
reasons: first-picking Nocturne is among the worst possible first picks: no OP champion taken, reveals the comp, lets T1 do what they want
Jax blinded top gets answered by Gragas, one of the best anti-melee/anti-dash top laners
G2 plan (Draven + Nautilus bot cheese) does not fit a Jax top; a Shen top with global ultimate would have fit a bot-focused plan
picks are individually meta but do not package together
T1's only weak point is Leona with no escape; Xayah-style self-peel would counter Nocturne

cases.label: KCB draft excellent, BDSA plan harder
reasons: KCB: coherent terrain + dive family (Maokai, Taliyah) with Draven to cash kills under tower; strong side bot / weak side top plan
KCB bans judged all logical (early AD bots, Pyke, Braum, Renata) - removes disengage against their dive
Small KCB errors: Viego belongs to no family without a reset/enchanter partner; Ornn is a scaling pick in an early-tempo comp
BDSA standard/meta picks (Renekton, Orianna, Volibear) with no clear identity
Bard on BDSA is a big mistake: a lone catcher with no second hard CC to follow up the ultimate

cases.label: BDSA cannot win lane, fight or scale
reasons: Jinx + Volibear self-locks BDSA: Jinx needs mobility/disengage (Tahm Kench, Karma, Lulu...), Volibear just hands out a free Zeri
Thresh brings no frontline and forces BDSA to ban catchers; blind Renekton was then countered by Rumble
BDSA has three short-range champions against Zeri - the worst matchup of the series
KCB: double terrain control (Taliyah, Rumble) and several disengage tools; Jax wins vs Volibear and outscales
Crescent-like KCB comp that can dive top and bot and outscales every lane

cases.label: GenG has all the tools
reasons: GenG: double global ultimate (Pantheon + TF) with stacked hard CC (Pantheon, TF, Bard) - catch comp built for the mid game
Seraphine + Ezreal are both immobile against a double-catch draft; JDG got baited into it
JDG comp is reactive, no proactive win condition; GenG is proactive and cyclic around Pantheon ultimate
Xin Zhao loses to Pantheon; TF outscales Aurora's burst
too many options to track on JDG side creates decision overload

cases.label: Veigar and Jarvan picks misplaced
reasons: first-pick Lulu answered by Vi + Yunara; GenG goes catch (Vi, Ahri, Rakan)
Jinx + Lulu are immobile against a catch comp
Veigar cannot play into Vi/Ahri/Rakan (Galio would have been far better); Jarvan has no targets vs mobile picks, Corki was needed
GenG mid-game comp with cyclic ultimates should beat JDG late-game scaling (Jinx, Veigar stacks)
Jinx takes mid lane so Veigar is pushed to side lanes and gets caught; Renekton vs Gnar is a 50-50 skill matchup

cases.label: G2 checkmated: no teamfight, no scaling
reasons: G2 first-picked Varus (immobile) with no guardian and left Pantheon open after Poppy was used - permanent weakness
Mundo jungle + tank top = double tank without an exponential carry; loses teamfights and scaling
Blind Gnar should be punished by a ranged on-hit top (Kennen AD, Nidalee, Jayce, Draven), but Pantheon's global ult covers the split, so G2 had to pick a tank
Gnar + Pantheon global ult is a strong map-pressure combo, like Gnar + Nocturne
G2 missed Taliyah (and Jarvan) which counter Sivir and would pair with Pantheon; banning LeBlanc made no sense

cases.label: clearly prefers HLE draft
reasons: HLE: Corki package should give drakes and objectives; Lucian brings bot pressure and wins the Azir interaction
FearX has a single tank (bot side), no tank on top side, and a comp that only works if Viego snowballs with resets
Viego was blind-picked and directly counter-picked by Poppy (invade + the disengage FearX lacked)
Gnar loses to Udyr/Corki and Azir cannot do much into Lucian: each FearX lane loses its matchup
Nami gives HLE scaling and lets them peel Corki late; Senna + Nautilus answer Lucian but Nautilus cannot tank him once scaled

cases.label: prefers HLE, Maokai tips it
reasons: HLE stacks terrain control (Maokai roots + Rumble ultimate, plus long-range damage): FearX has no space to play
bold counter-picks: Tristana into Azir and Rumble into Udyr, even though Udyr is usually good against Rumble
FearX improved on game 1: Azir + Kalista is much better for Nashor fights, and Kalista + Renata is strong early
HLE is weaker in lane (Milio brings nothing early), so their plan is to survive and scale towards drakes
without the Maokai he would have preferred FearX

cases.label: strongly prefers KT draft
reasons: KT: Orianna first pick, then Vi for a Vi + Orianna double catch combo (ball on Vi, both ultimates stack)
Udyr counters Rumble and is the top tank; Senna gives range and Ornn the second tank: slow, long-fight comp that controls space
KDF took Rumble mainly to deny it, Viego only answers Vi and is bad into Udyr; Maokai would have been far better
after banning 8 ADCs KDF ended with a blind ADC in pick 4 and no tank outside support: they trapped themselves
Orianna speed/shield on Senna lets KT buy time and outscale

cases.label: KT drafts by families, KDF trolled
reasons: KT opens a family with Orianna, then adds Nocturne: Orianna ball + Nocturne's global ult gives an unavoidable pick combo
Udyr side lane + Nocturne global gives KT an instant 1-3-1 / lane-assignment edge; Azir is poor in side lane
KDF's Rumble gave Udyr for free; their mid answer should have been a tank or tank-catcher (Ornn, Galio) to combo with Vi
Caitlyn + Hwei double range bot stops KDF from taking a melee tank support (Maokai), so KDF ends with no tank
caveat: full-range catch comps are very hard to execute and need good wave management; Hwei slightly anti-synergic (no disengage)

cases.label: G2 smarter, Ivern opens carry win conditions
reasons: TES first-picked Varus after anti-mobility bans (Zac, Poppy) and built a scaling range core (Varus + Azir) - a fine but passive plan
G2 delayed the jungle pick, then took Ivern: an enchanter jungle that boosts Tristana and then Camille, creating a mid and a top carry win condition
Kalista + Leona bot lane dives from level 1-2 and snowballs; Tristana gives mid priority to control drakes
TES weak spots: Nautilus a little redundant (Braum or another catcher would add more) and Xin Zhao improvable
Chinese teams are aggressive but struggle to play slow scaling Azir games; G2's unusual picks force them off their scripts

cases.label: JDG draft well thought out
reasons: LNG finally took Vi + Ahri catch, but must land about 5 picks between minutes 8 and 20 or they lose automatically
Neeko is a strong answer to Ahri + Vi: matches push and gives disengage; Rakan can engage or disengage
Wukong outscales Vi (multi-target catches late); Aatrox outvalues K'Sante in fights
Tristana has no peel (Nautilus support); Ashe would have added another catch tool
catch comps on long cooldowns (Ahri, Vi) are weak defensively compared with Blitzcrank/Pyke-style catch

cases.label: G2 near-perfect draft, TES self-countered
reasons: TES first-picked Draven as an aggro answer to scaling, but G2 immediately locked Kog'Maw + Braum; Braum is a historical hard counter to Draven (wall eats the axes)
TES draft is incoherent: short-range immobile lane bully (Draven) mixed with a long-range mobile late-game poke mid (Corki); a Draven plan wants mid priority and a bot dive, not Corki
Jarvan into Kog'Maw is a false counter: Kog'Maw is never picked without a peeler, and Braum's shield/ult splits any Jarvan engage
G2 favoured in every lane except an even mid: positive bot and top matchups plus far better scaling; Kog'Maw strong at 5, broken at 7-9
Only flaw for G2: Twisted Fate top instead of Shen; TF creates a win condition that is also a lose condition (Jarvan can catch him), Shen's global shield would have secured the scaling plan
TES has only two paths: punish Kog'Maw in the first three cycles (G2 can just sit under tower) or play around catching TF - neither likely enough

cases.label: KCorp cascade of bad picks
reasons: KCorp on red side never answered the Maokai first pick with a faster-farming jungler (Lillia, Karthus, Brand) to out-scale it
Zeri is poor into Maokai saplings and has no frontline to hit; Sivir or Kai'Sa would have handled it better
Xin Zhao is anti-synergistic with Azir (one wants passive scaling, the other early activity) and loses to Maokai at objectives
Banning Renekton instead of Tristana, then Yuumi, left KCorp with no tank and forced Canna onto a passive K'Sante instead of a strong-side carry
SK: Lucian + Nami lane wins early and scales; Taliyah + Maokai double terrain control for Nashor/setup; Gnar blind with a TP lead
KCorp's Azir/Zeri/Yuumi damage cannot reach SK's ranged lineup - big DPS on paper, nothing to hit in fights

cases.label: KC draft not thought through
reasons: KC first-picked Lucian to win lanes early; against a better team he prefers a scaling, counter-less pick (Azir, flex Ryze)
Fnatic answered Aphelios + Milio, denying the Lucian-Milio combo and outscaling; KC then took Nami instead of Nautilus (hard engage counters Milio and gives a frontline)
No tank: an Azir comp needs DPS + frontline for Baron setups; Nami gives neither
Blind Gragas top loses to K'Sante and to Akali; KC can win no lane in lane assignment, leaving only jungle carry or scaling
Akali counters Azir in side lane after 14 minutes; Fnatic's K'Sante is a top-tier objective/Baron champion that KC did not ban

cases.label: G2 draft 9-10/10, KC unprepared
reasons: KC repeated Lucian and blinded Milio; G2 answered Aphelios + Nautilus, the hard-engage counter to Milio
LeBlanc for Caps was left open: KC had no ban or prepared answer (K'Sante would have been his choice)
KC loses all three lanes on paper; their only angle is the level-6 ultimate combo (Malphite, Neeko, Vi, Lucian)
Malphite is not a counter to Kennen (energy cannot be drained, Kennen outranges); Jarvan IV, Yorick or Zac were the real answers
Again no real tank in the first picks; Milio does nothing for drake/Herald/tower setups in the current larva meta

cases.label: KC draft 0/20, cannot see a win
reasons: Vi first pick is an anti-dash pick, yet KC banned the dashers (Corki, etc.) - picks and bans are disconnected
Vi + Rakan + Kai'Sa: no tank, no synergy, the 'trinity' of picks that should never meet
Kai'Sa (short range, weak wave clear) loses to double-range Seraphine + Senna bot, which shoves and pokes under tower
Akali left open into Azir; Giants' faked Yone pre-pick then Seraphine was a mind game that worked
only plan: Azir + K'Sante Nash control (K'Sante clears the jungler) - one tool only, and KC did not play it
Giants stronger mid game, scaling and teamfight; KC loses lanes, scaling and fights

cases.label: KC comp has nothing that fits
reasons: Taliyah first pick is a 'bridge' champion that needs a partner (dive bot or siege comp); with Senna + Ornn bot it gives nothing
Fnatic answers with Hwei (long range, wave clear, a 'useful Taliyah') and a blind Ivern for scaling
Rek'Sai is weak vs straight-line skillshots (Hwei, Milio, Morgana) and cannot help any lane
Jax picked last after banning Camille/TF, blind and unsupported; Poppy blocks him for 25 minutes
Fnatic: triple frontline block (Poppy, Ivern/Daisy, Nautilus) + Zeri/Hwei damage - wins drakes and phase 2 easily
KC over-commits draft to Canna and forgets Upset

cases.label: KT too much scaling, bad Gnar blind
reasons: KT stacked scaling (Azir, Smolder, Rell) without an early bridge jungler like Xin or Lee Sin
Gnar blind-picked into Kiin: many ranged tops punish it and he answered with Tristana
Gen.G combine early snowball (Tristana + Nautilus invade, Lee Sin) with scaling (Corki, Zeri)
Smolder has no self-peel, so point-and-click CC like Nautilus is the best answer
Gen.G bans removed Xin Zhao and K'Sante, KT's bridge options

cases.label: about 75/25 for AL at draft
reasons: blind Pantheon first pick is strong once Poppy is gone, and it denies split-push picks (Yone, Sylas)
Gen.G should have sent Aurora top into Rumble and taken a ranged mid (Orianna) against Annie
Jhin has no synergy and only patches a range problem; Kai'Sa would have followed up Alistar CC
Xin Zhao rated a weak, scrim-inflated jungle pick in slow official games
Gen.G should have taken Sylas instead of Alistar; red side keeps getting out-drafted

cases.label: first balanced draft, 55/45 AL
reasons: AL plays slower around Varus, Bard and Sion ultimates, with a tank nobody on Gen.G can kill
Gen.G is a full catch/explosive comp (Ambessa + Vi + Rakan, Ziggs follow-up) that wants to kill Varus and Bard
Gen.G lacks frontline; explosive combos peak at 15-25 minutes before tanks come online
Akali should handle Taliyah and Ziggs and can split fights - but she can either 1v9 or be locked down

cases.label: 70/30 AL, Jarvan left open
reasons: Gen.G left Jarvan open against an immobile Caitlyn + Karma lane - a capital ban mistake
AL chains ultimates: Jarvan into Galio, Miss Fortune, Neeko and Smolder ult
Smolder top punishes melee tanks; AL counter-picked it into K'Sante, the best possible Smolder matchup
stacking win condition: 200 Smolder stacks at 20 minutes is close to an auto-win; Gen.G must take Drake 3/4 or Nashor first
Rek'Sai or Volibear top would have been better answers than K'Sante

cases.label: simpler draft for KC, wins late
reasons: KC: safe first-pick Azir, solid lane holds, scales - wins once everyone has 3-4 items
KCB: catch comp (Vi + Taliyah + Varus + Nautilus) that is ultimate-dependent and strongest from level 6 to 1-2 items
He prefers Varus over Ezreal at ADC, but every other position favours KC
Aatrox into Sion is an outdated pick: the matchup has favoured Sion for months and Aatrox cannot kill him
Vi links well with Taliyah but lacks the damage to kill Sion and is weak into Azir

cases.label: for KT: T1 lost on Renekton
reasons: T1 blind-picked Renekton; K'Sante (and Ornn) are the known matchups Renekton cannot play into
Viego (a reset champion) makes no sense into a turbo-tank comp; an anti-tank (Lillia, Cassiopeia, Master Yi) was needed
T1 have no answer to Dr. Mundo: tanky scaling, takes drakes, nobody can kill him
KT: Alistar first pick for tempo, Syndra + Corki give early pressure to secure every drake

cases.label: biggest draft gap of the final
reasons: Kalista first pick has no answer (only Draven); Kalista + Renata dive every objective
Trundle first pick is a reactive champion and bad into Kalista
Nocturne punishes Cassiopeia (made for that) and cancels any carry top
Anivia is strong into Tahm Kench; Gragas top counters Jayce and blocks KT's siege plan
KT siege comp has no real poke: Caitlyn alone, Mordekaiser pointless

cases.label: clearly for NIP, balanced comp
reasons: NIP: Nami gives double value, able to amplify either Lucian or Corki; Corki + Lucian give mid and bot priority (invade, early drakes)
WBG bot: Zeri + Lulu does not fit the rest of the comp and gets poked hard by Lucian; Zeri does little in fights
NIP tank jungle (Sejuani) outscales the opposing jungler and allows flexible objective setups
Kennen consolidates NIP's mid game, even if he dislikes the Kennen-into-Rumble lane (Doran's Blade, slow start)
WBG comp is otherwise standard: bridging jungler, scaling bot, top lane on its own

cases.label: DK wins early, MAD slightly better late
reasons: DK: Syndra + Lee Sin duo should win mid/jungle early, and that mid pressure indirectly protects Gwen top
MAD plan: Orianna + Gragas (flex jungle/top) to hold the line and survive into scaling, not to win early
Gwen should beat Gnar in lane and especially in side lane; MAD has no real answer to Gwen splitting
both comps are strong in pure teamfight; he gives MAD a slight late edge, but it depends on their ADC's item timing
draft mistake: MAD should have banned Gwen against Khan instead of spending bans on other top picks

cases.label: tanks win fights, Poppy counters Jax
reasons: After the first rotation he preferred the right side (scaling, range, Nashor) except for a weak level 1-6 window
Second rotation flipped it: left took two tanks (Poppy, Udyr) while right blind-picked Jax and Gnar with no frontline
Teamfight theory: tanks win teamfights, and Poppy counters Jax in the 2v2 around lanes
Lucian first pick is an early-only pick that decays after about level 7
If right does not win lanes hard, it has no chance

cases.label: right wins by far, even more than game 1
reasons: Right has triple scaling, sustained DPS and a strong terrain-control mid (Taliyah)
Udyr proxy buys early pushes top; Vi gives catch; Aphelios allows fast Nashor
Left has no burst for Nashor, no tank, no wave clear - full fly-style aggression he dislikes
Lucian first pick again gave the Milio + Aphelios combo to the opponent
Jax into Udyr does not work until very late; Kennen or Trundle would answer Udyr

cases.label: KC draft lost before the game
reasons: KC left Nocturne open and then picked Camille and Ryze, both weak into a Nocturne global ultimate
Ryze cannot teamfight into Orianna and cannot side-lane with Nocturne hunting him; Orianna ball on Nocturne is a ready-made dive combo
KC drafted catch tools (blind Camille, Ziggs follow-up) while they are the side that will be caught - should play defence
two pure DPS (Vayne, Ryze) with no real tank: Camille in place of a frontliner leaves the comp unbalanced; Wukong has nothing to do
Liquid have reset/teamfight tools (Tristana, Orianna, Rell) - KC must avoid 5v5 and play 1-3-1 / fast tower breaking

cases.label: KC: no damage, no tank, wrong jungle
reasons: KC cannot kill Ornn and lack an anti-tank pick; Trundle was open and was the ideal answer (anti-tank, punishes immobile Mel and Pantheon, pillar cancels dashes)
KC chose Jarvan IV over Trundle/better picks and banned damage they themselves needed
Lee Sin + Yasuo is an old but strong mid-jungle 2v2 combo (targeted kick into Yasuo ultimate) that controls the centre of the map
Ornn breaks Anivia walls and scales into a strong frontline
KC's real win condition was catching the immobile Mel with Jarvan; they took ~20 minutes to understand it

cases.label: T1 draft on another planet
reasons: T1 turtle comp: Braum + Xin Zhao wall protecting an out-ranging Caitlyn; Ornn holds Rumble and buys time
BLG's only plan is to kill Faker; Viktor terrain control punishes short-range Wukong engages
Ezreal into Caitlyn is a known losing matchup (crit scales better than ability-haste range); Jhin was the right answer
Annie first pick is inflated (8-0) because nobody countered it with range; Annie + Rumble are only scary until mid game
once outer towers fall the map enters an economic farming phase that favours T1's scaling

cases.label: slight preference for T1's Nashor comp
reasons: T1: their signature Nashor comp - two DPS, a fast-Nashor jungler (Zyra), a tank top and Alistar to push enemies away
Zeri adds magic damage to a double-ADC draft (Tristana mid), farms fast and can secure Nashor at 20 minutes
KT: double range (Azir + Ezreal) with a strong teamfight block - Braum blocks engages and Ezreal/Viego can reset fights
KT plays full anti-engage while T1 does not really engage and just wants to farm
K'Sante picked into Skarner to keep the top side roughly even

cases.label: instantly for JDG, bot win condition
reasons: JDG: tanky disengage/scaling block (Maokai, K'Sante, Braum) to protect Jinx and win the bot side
BLG win condition is top (Fiora at 3 items) vs JDG bot - the bot side usually wins because it converts to drakes and Nash
Alistar is a draft error: engage into an anti-engage comp; Bard would have punished an immobile Jinx
BLG wants early dives bot and to hold 25 minutes until Fiora spikes
JDG's Renekton last pick vs Fiora disliked (K'Sante top or a real Fiora counter preferred)
lanes partly swapped in game (Ahri top) - role assignment approximate

cases.label: G2 draft favored, ~70/30 if equal teams
reasons: G2 mid-jungle (Aurora + Pantheon) stronger, Ezreal + Leona strong in 2v2 and into Annie/Alistar
BLG has nothing to reach Ezreal: once he has 3-4 items G2 wins teamfights; G2 has many tools (Pantheon, Leona, Ornn ults) to kill/cancel Miss Fortune
plan: Ornn blocks top risk-free, Pantheon roams top-to-bot, stall until Ezreal items
draft mistakes by G2: left Rumble open to Bin (a signature pick, Ornn answer is ~60/40 for Rumble), gave Alistar to ON, did not take Sylas against first-pick Annie
bias note: he criticises G2 for drafting as if they were as strong as China instead of around their strengths

cases.label: joke draft, no match possible
reasons: G2 first-picked Vi while Taliyah was open: Knight gets his best pick (seen unbeaten in LPL), Skarner beats Vi
Ahri into Knight's Taliyah repeats a scenario already lost many times in China
Jax blind into Bin (Sion), a matchup Bin knows perfectly; no tank in G2 draft and no damage plan
pure-top Jax needs a safe bot (enchanter/tank, cross-map ult like Senna or Karthus) or a very aggressive bot; G2 had neither, lanes not connected
Sion + Karma shields + Skarner: mathematically G2 cannot burst BLG's front line

cases.label: coherent G2 draft, both sides decent
reasons: G2 finally drafts a sensible plan: Olaf top into Renekton backed by two cross-map ults (TF, Senna)
BLG shows champion families: Veigar + Poppy cage-and-push like Veigar + Alistar
Trundle pillar interrupts Poppy ult and is good vs immobiles, but Nocturne + TF (double global) would have been stronger; G2 lacks a real tank and should have removed Braum
the plan needs an early invade and a level-6 TF gank top; G2 did not execute and drifted bot (late: Olaf useless, game unwinnable)

cases.label: dislikes G2's unclear, tankless draft
reasons: G2 has no clear identity: catch (Neeko) without follow-up, double carry (Tristana + MF) with zero tank
Nunu + MF answer to Wukong is very poor: two channeled ults into instant CC; Xin/Rakan-type picks would have answered Wukong
Tristana is weak at 2 items and mid game, so G2 will lose drakes and map control before scaling
Nunu wants to play bot for dragons while the top laner plays a carry - lanes not connected
Ambessa vs Jax is still favourable for G2 top

cases.label: G2 checkmated KC in draft
reasons: G2 double-stack plan: Nasus jungle + Senna both stack, ~20 gold per stack, an economy gap that wins by itself if unpunished
